chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who performs Hajj and dedicates his Hajj and Umrah, or part of his circumambulation, for one of his family members, while he is absent from him in another city. I said, 'Will that reduce his reward?' He said, 'No. It is for him and for his companion, and for him is a reward besides that with what he has linked.' I said, 'And if he is deceased, does that enter upon him?' He said, 'Yes, to the extent that if he is under Wrath, it is forgiven for him, or if there is constriction upon him, it is expanded upon him.' I said, 'So he, in his place, knows that that deed has reached him?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And even if he was a Nasibi (hostile one), does that benefit him?' He said, 'Yes. It is lightened from him.'

key_terms.نَاصِب: Nasibi (one hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Can a living person perform Hajj on behalf of a deceased relative and share the reward?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that dedicating Hajj or Umrah to absent or deceased relatives is valid, with the reward shared between the performer and the dedicatee. It further establishes that these acts can alleviate punishment or expand one's standing in the afterlife, even for those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt, demonstrating the universal efficacy of ritual devotion in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I asked himasws about the man who performs Hajj, so he makes his Hajj and his Umra, or part of his circumambulation for one of his family members, and he is absent from him in another city. I said, ‘So would that effect a reduction from his Recompense?’ Heasws said: ‘No. It would be for him and for his companion; and for him would be a recompense besides that with what he has linked’. I said, ‘And he is deceased, would that enter upon him?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, to the extent that if he happens to be under Wrath, so it would be Forgiven for him, or if there happens to be a constriction upon him, so it would be Expanded upon him’. I said, ‘So he, in his place, would know that, that deed was performed for his right?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘And even if he was a Nasibi (Hostile one), that would benefit him?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes. It (Punishment) would be Lightened from him’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who assigns his al-Hajj or al-‘Umrah or part of his Tawaf for his family who is absent in some other land; if it reduces from his reward. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is for him and his companion, and he will have additional rewards because of maintaining good relation.’ I then asked, ‘If that party is dead will it reach him?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, even if that party is subject to anger, he will be forgiven or if he is under pressure, he will be relieved.’ I then asked, ‘Will he notice that such a deed has approached him?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he will notice.’ I then asked, ‘Even if he is hostile to ’A’immah, will it benefit him?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it will provide him relief.’”
